function: Jointly optimizes BS transmit precoding and discrete RIS phase shifts to maximize energy efficiency of RIS-assisted RSMA, using two alternating quantum-circuit learning models (pp. 1, 7).
system: Downlink one-layer RSMA, BS with 2 antennas, 2 single-antenna users, reflecting single-connected RIS with N=4 elements and 10-bit discrete phases; carrier frequency not stated (pp. 4, 10).
method: Two variational quantum circuits with reduced-input encoding, unsupervised energy-efficiency loss, parameter-shift gradient descent, trained alternately (precoder, then RIS); run with IBM Qiskit (pp. 7-11).
data_channel: Custom simulation: LoS plus NLoS BS-RIS channel and LoS RIS-user channel after [34], 5G path-loss model [43], shadow fading, random angles; no dataset (pp. 5, 10).
test_conditions: Ntrain=100 training iterations, one channel sample H(t) per iteration; results over transmit SNR 2-28 dB for one setup (N=4, Nuser=2, NTx=2); no unseen scenario (pp. 10-12).
baselines: Non-learned: conventional matched-filter precoding with cosine-similarity RIS phases; random precoding and random RIS phases. Learned: alternative quantum circuit model (QCNN-style, ref. [46]) (pp. 11-13).
metrics: Energy efficiency (bps/Hz/J) versus transmit SNR; training loss versus iteration (convergence); qubit counts; complexity order of encoding (pp. 11-12).
complexity: Encoding stage O(N) for quantum reduced-input versus O((Nuser+NTx)N) for classical input layer; qubits needed Nuser+Nreduce+N (RIS model) and Nuser+Nreduce+NTx (precoder) (pp. 11-12).
q1_support: p. 5: "components representing outdoor conditions, can be modeled as [34]"; p. 10: "following the 5G path loss model [43]". Custom statistical simulator; no 3GPP TR 38.901 profile, QuaDRiGa, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 10: "The following parameters were considered for the RIS-assisted RSMA communication system: N = 4, κ = 2, Nuser = 2, NTx = 2". Fig. 6 (p. 12) varies only the transmit SNR; no other scenario, size or band is tested.
q3_support: p. 11: "a conventional optimization method employing matched filter (MF) for the BS precoding [44] and cosine similarity approach for the RIS phase shifting [45] is adopted"; "The proposed approach also outperforms the alternative quantum model described previously".
q4_support: p. 12: "we compare the computational time complexity of the Reduced-Input encoding" (O(N) quantum versus O((Nuser+NTx)N) classical input layer); qubit counts on pp. 11-12. Only the encoding stage is analysed.
q5_support: p. 10: "This section analyzes numerical results of the Monte-Carlo simulations showcasing the merits of the proposed QML framework". Data come from the authors' own simulation; the paper gives no code or data link and uses no public dataset.
notes: Area 3: the trained quantum models output the BS precoder and the RIS phases. q3 counts the authors' alternative quantum circuit (QCNN-style, single output qubit, ref. [46], p. 11 footnote 14) as the learned baseline; it shares the unsupervised framework of Algorithm 1, so the reviewer should confirm it is not a variant of the proposed model. q4 rests on the encoding-stage complexity and qubit counts only, not on a full-method analysis. Very small setup (4 RIS elements, 2 users).
